commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Flatten MLP tokens locally under context parallelism (#10145)

The shared and routed MLPs now flatten `[B, S, D]` into tokens inside a
`shard_map`. Each device flattens its own block of rows and sequence
shard, so no data moves between devices. `_unflatten_tokens` reverses
the flatten and restores the residual layout.

The old flatten used a global `(b s)` rearrange. Under context
parallelism with more than one row per batch shard, it needed an
all-to-all each way in every layer. Without context sharding, the token
order does not change. With it, each expert-parallel group gets one
sequence slice of each row instead of whole rows. This changes which
tokens a full expert drops.

A CPU test checks that CP2 logits equal CP1 logits when no token drops.
The compiled CP2 forward has 4 all-to-alls instead of 8.

On one GB200 rack at 65K context on CP4/EP16, restored from hero step
240000 (106 steps per arm):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| step time | 15.938 s | 15.586 s (+2.26% tokens/s) |
| drop fraction | 1.17% | 0.23% |
| loss | | −2.3e-3 |

With #10121, CP4 takes 14.626 s per step against 15.137 s and 1.94%
drops on CP1. At 262K on CP4/EP16, each device holds one row, so the
compiled program does not change.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Reject model requests after the attempt deadline (#10303)

When a harness caught cancellation at the attempt deadline, it could
keep requesting model turns until a limit stopped it. The engine then
graded and returned the rollout without a failure.[^1]

After the attempt deadline, each `ModelSession` request raises
`CancelledError`, as a request does when its transport caught the
cancellation. Without this, a harness that retries on `RolloutEnded`
does not stop, because the attempt deadline cancels the task only one
time. If the harness ends after the attempt deadline with a refusal or
no error, the attempt fails as `attempt` with a `TimeoutError`, and the
engine does not grade it. A harness that raises its own error after the
deadline fails with that error, as it does after a turn deadline.

[^1]: The engine before #10203 had the same gap.

---

description](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10303#issuecomment-6277815876)

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Replace task sessions with registered harnesses (#10203)

RolloutEngine runs each task attempt through a harness, which owns the
agent loop and calls the model through a `ModelSession`.
`RolloutEngine(machine_factories, harnesses, *, observer=None)` holds
the two registries, and `run_task(spec, model, *, run_id=None)` returns
a `GradedRollout(rollout, grade)`. `Rollout` replaces `RolloutData`: it
holds `run_id`, one `ConversationRecord` for each conversation of the
attempt, the stop reason, metrics, and run outputs, and no longer
carries `task_id` or the grade. Without a `run_id`, each attempt gets a
new random ID, so the events of repeated attempts of a task stay apart.

A harness implements `Harness`: `check(task, limits)` rejects a task
before any machine starts, and `run(context, session)` runs one attempt
with a `HarnessContext(task, machine, events, cleanup, run_id)`. This
replaces `TaskSession`, `TaskSessionFactory`, and `TaskGrader`. The
session's `start(prompt)` begins a conversation, `reply(observations,
token_ids=...)` continues it, and `record(observations=..., data=...,
metrics=...)` adds to the step of the last turn. The session records the
exact tokens and applies `max_turns`, `max_total_tokens`, the length
stop, `model_turn_timeout`, `tool_turn_timeout`, and
`total_turn_timeout`. The next request after a limit raises
`LimitReached`, and a failed model request raises `RolloutEnded` with
the model's error as its cause. After either, `record(data=...,
metrics=...)` still adds to the step of the last turn until the record
is final, for example a final reward. Without a turn, `record` raises
the refusal again. A second `start` is a new conversation, so
`Transition.reset` and the engine's reset rules are removed, and the
rollout keeps every conversation. Harnesses do not grade.
`SessionGrader` and harness grading are removed, the engine grades the
last conversation that has a model turn with the task's grader, and a
harness puts its own rewards in step data. Thus a new conversation whose
first request fails leaves the earlier one to grade.
`harness_rollout(harness, task, model, *, limits, machine=None, ...)`
runs a harness without the engine, and `task_machine(task, factory,
runtime, *, cleanup_timeout)` starts a task machine for it.

`ShellHarness(command_timeout=..., shell_tool=..., tools=...)` takes the
shell options and tool providers that were in the spec and the engine,
so one engine can register several shell configurations.
`StepHarness(open_episode)` runs a step-style `Episode` (`prepare`,
`advance`, `close`). `AgentHarness(agent)` replaces `AgentTaskSession`.
Each `complete` call of the agent runs the session in the caller's task,
with no queue and no request tasks. One model request can be open at a
time. A call that is cancelled while the model generates loses that
generation and does not change the record, and the last prompt again
gets the same turn. After the attempt ends, calls wait until the
cleanup, after grading, so a waiting agent does not change the task
machine during grading. The cleanup then cancels the agent, and an agent
that does not stop within `cleanup_timeout` is a cleanup error.

The core types (records, specs, events, and exceptions) are in
`rolloutengine.models`, which replaces `rolloutengine.contracts` and
`rolloutengine.spec`. The harness contract is in
`rolloutengine.harness.core`. The built-in harnesses are in
`rolloutengine.harness.shell`, `rolloutengine.harness.external`
(`AgentHarness`), and `rolloutengine.harness.step`.
`rolloutengine.validation` replaces `rolloutengine.checks`.

When the harness ends or a turn deadline expires, the record is final.
The session cancels a model call that is still open, for example in an
agent's HTTP handler, and ignores its result, so the grader and the
returned rollout see the same record. A harness registers the close of
its resources with `context.cleanup`. The closes run after grading, each
within `cleanup_timeout`, and a failure is a cleanup error of the
attempt.

`TaskRolloutSpec(task, harness, task_machine, verifier_machine, limits,
trace, judge_connection)` replaces `LoweredTaskSpec`, `TaskRuntimeSpec`,
and `TaskSessionSpec`. Its `limits`, a `RolloutLimits`, holds the turn,
token, and time limits of `TaskSessionSpec`.
`RolloutEngine.check(spec)`, which `run_task` also calls first, replaces
`lower_task` and `validate_lowered_task`. `Prompt` replaces
`SessionStart`. `ModelRequest.continuation`, a
`Continuation(served_token_ids, assistant_message_index)`, replaces
`prefix_token_ids` and `assistant_message_index`. A request has a
continuation, pinned `prompt_token_ids`, or neither, and a `MESSAGES`
rollout never has a continuation. Under `EXACT_TOKENS`, `reply` refuses
pinned tokens that do not start with the served tokens before it sends
the request. In `Transition`, `token_ids` replaces
`next_prompt_token_ids`, and `next_options` is removed, so options
change only with a new conversation. `reward`, `token_rewards`,
`token_credit`, `reward_components`, and the per-step `grade` are
removed from `Transition`. A harness can put such values in its new
`data` field, which the engine keeps unchanged. A trainer that reads
per-token rewards from it compares their length with the turn's
`response_token_ids`; `RolloutStep.response_end` is the index of the
turn's last response token. `check` also rejects, for every harness, a
shell binding without a task machine, as it already did for the shell
capability, and a graded `state` task, because the engine does not
capture state.

A judge grader grades on the host through `grade_remote_judge_answer`,
the function that the curation pipelines use, with `judge_connection` or
with `VERIFYIT_JUDGE_BASE_URL` and `VERIFYIT_JUDGE_API_KEY`. It uses no
verifier machine. `judge_connection` holds an API key, so `model_dump`,
JSON, and pickle leave it out. `check` rejects a judge task with a
verifier machine, a judge task with no connection and no
`VERIFYIT_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, a judge task with no `JudgeSpec.model` and no
`VERIFYIT_JUDGE_MODEL`, and a judge task whose answer is not in the
conversation. The verifier deadline stops only the engine's wait for a
host judge. Each judge request has `JudgeSpec.request_timeout`, and for
every rubric except labels the OpenAI client retries a failed request up
to two times (#10246).

An interrupted attempt raises `RolloutInterrupted(rollout, operation)`
from `harness_rollout`, and `GradedRolloutInterrupted`, with the grade
of the completed turns, from `run_task`. A model failure still grades
the completed turns, and a harness that returns with no model turn fails
with `prepare`. `RolloutContractError` means only a token-contract
violation.

The token trace grows its loss mask and log probabilities as lists, and
the rollout is built once at the end. With a fake model that costs
nothing, engine time per turn falls from 2.4–2.5 to 1.0–1.1 ms at 129k
tokens and from 4.7–5.0 to 2.6 ms at 257k tokens (three runs each
against 24aa43cea).

MarinSkyRL pins rolloutengine at a Marin commit, so it keeps working
until it advances that pin. Its port must:

- run its step-style sessions through `StepHarness`, and put each old
`grade()` result in the last step's data. A session that computes that
result only at the end needs its own harness, which records it with
`record(data=...)` after `LimitReached` or a failed model request
- give Nemotron its own harness, which calls `start` again for its
correction turn
- read `rollout.conversations` when it builds training samples
- register one shell harness for each shell configuration
- import from the new modules
- build its `ChatContinuation` from `ModelRequest.continuation`
- read `result.rollout` and `result.grade` from `run_task`, and `grade`
from `GradedRolloutInterrupted`
- take task IDs from its specs, and rebuild its stored task Parquet
files, which hold `LoweredTaskSpec` JSON
- replace the grader of each stored task that has a `SessionGrader`
(`kind: "session"`), which no longer parses
- drop `RolloutOperation.CLEANUP`, which the engine never raised

Observers get `run_id` instead of `run_key`, `ConversationStarted` for
each conversation instead of `SessionPrepared`, `TransitionCompleted`
without `reset_conversation`, and the cleanup steps `episode_close`,
`agent_stop`, and `tool_provider_close` instead of `session_close`.

Part of #10187.

---------

Co-authored-by: Rafal Wojdyla <ravwojdyla@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Reduce forwarding serialization and decompression work (#10271)

Reduce forwarding work by skipping oversized parent IPC encodes, sharing
immutable payloads across retry clones, and moving the hub's owned
request buffer into Arrow decoding. Decode complete zstd frames with a
known content size into a bounded output buffer. Other zstd frame
formats retain the existing decoder; gzip and streaming providers retain
their existing behavior.

Keep SQL reads, compression level 1, serial log ordering, the wire
format, and durable cursor settlement.

On five rotating local replays per variant, median delivery of 1M
synthetic rows increased from 284k/sec on main to 409k/sec (1.44×). With
only the encoding and copy changes, the same cohort measured 361k/sec.
Adding the decoder change reduced median cumulative write/RPC time per
replay, across two serial requests, from 1,391 to 1,243 ms. Source and
authenticated hub shared four CPUs with release builds, production
jemalloc/zstd, warm Parquet source files, and local-disk durability. The
decoder comparison's throughput ranges overlap. These runs exclude TLS,
cold remote objects, concurrent queries, fleet hub load, and steady
small-write coalescing.

[Final measurements and
reproduction](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10271#issuecomment-6275161594).
[RPC diagnosis and profiling
evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10271#issuecomment-6274803649).

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: muchanem
commits.message:
[taskforge] Add the stage coordinator over the build DAG (#10087)

Add `stage_coordinator`, which runs an item through triage, author,
build, validate and review with the stage functions a caller passes in
`StageFunctions`. Each stage returns an event with an exit, and a
transition table gives the next stage. The item's state is a fold over
its events (`derive_state`). `ItemBudget` bounds build revisions and
validation retries, and the coordinator spends them when it records
`AUTHOR_FAILED`, `BUILD_FAILED` or `DECIDED`. A build error from the
program's own code, `BuildFailure` or any other exception, costs a
revision. `BuildInfrastructureFailure` (the build host failed: a sandbox
did not start, an image did not pull, a pod died), `ModelUnavailable`
and `OSError` (a storage fault, a missing blob or memo) are failures the
author cannot fix. Those fail the item in place at the build stage, and
the next `run_item` builds the same program again with its revisions
unspent. When the author raises `StructuredOutputError` because its
structured reply stayed invalid after the repair turn, as when the
output limit cut it, the coordinator records `AUTHOR_FAILED`, spends a
revision from the same budget, and asks the author again with
`Revision(AUTHOR_FAILURE, ...)`.

The `OPENED` event records the digests of the proposal and the budget,
and the coordinator's model digest, the model part of every step key. A
relaunch with any of them changed raises `ValueError`, so every build of
an item runs under one model. The author returns an `AuthoredProgram`,
the program with the Python source it came from. The coordinator writes
the source to `rounds/<n>/authored/<k>/program.py`, beside the manifest
`program.json`, with `k` the item's build failures so far. The build
stage loads the program from that file with
`StageFunctions.load_program`, so a sampling model author is called once
per revision. Each author call gets its own directory, so a process
killed after re-authoring leaves the program of the saved `AUTHORED`
event in place for the relaunch. `stage30_author/loader.py` is the plain
loader; the author PR replaces it with a restricted one (allowed
imports, safe builtins). A program defined in Python, as `static_author`
returns, has no source, and for it the build stage asks the author
again. In both cases a build whose program digest differs from the
`AUTHORED` event raises.

Events stay in an `ItemEventLog` (in memory here) while the item runs.
When the item reaches a terminal, `run_item` saves the log through an
`ItemEventStore`. `JsonEventStore` writes `items/<item_id>/events.json`
after every other file of the item, and the next `run_item` with an
empty log restores the log from it. An accepted or rejected item then
returns without running a stage or writing a byte. When the store lacks
the final log, as after a failed save retried with the same in-memory
log, `run_item` saves it before returning. An abandoned item re-enters
validation with its retries reset, and a failed item resumes at the
stage that raised, with the step store under `<root>/store` serving the
build steps already run. A process killed mid-item restarts from the
last saved terminal, or from triage. The ledger PR adds a file-backed
log saving each event on append.

The triage verdict and the review `Decision` types come along as the
vocabulary the machine records; `Retry.cause` and `Modify.findings` are
strings until validate returns. Validate and review are caller
functions: the coordinator writes the validate summary to
`validation.json` and passes review the JSON read back from it.
`stage_coordinator` sits above the numbered stages and may import every
one of them, and nothing imports it. The capability experiment runs a
catalog entry through the coordinator with its example program as a
sink-only build, to an accepted task.

The design is cut from draft #9993, and the base is #10081.

---------

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.message:
[marina] Add the public Snowball model family tree

Add a public Marina applet for the Snowball 67B A2B checkpoint family, with 130 model/run nodes, 138 parent edges, experiment evidence and scoped compute estimates. The tree supports expansion, zoom, search and branch filtering. Merge checkpoints show every pinned parent; the cooldown-family timeline records date provenance separately from weight ancestry.

The graph includes the campaign-1 serial merges, campaign-2 and campaign-3 DARE merges, BFCL recovery and protocol FTPO checkpoints, and the Smartie RL continuation. The Smartie chain is campaign-2 DARE-TIES-02 → .32 step 14 → .45 step 2 → .47 step 8 → .49 step 12. The .32 and .45 runs start fresh optimizers; .47 and .49 resume optimizer state. The displayed continuation step counts start at .45 update 1 and exclude .32's 14 updates. Internal checkpoints are distinguished from public releases. The .32 export is the best surviving checkpoint by pass@1 on its repeatedly inspected native development panel; the .49 export is user-selected with incomplete evaluation coverage. Pinned model cards, configs and W&B records support those distinctions.

The package declares its stable applet UUID and documents `marina release` from clean current main. Builds reject duplicate IDs, absent parents, cycles and cross-cooldown parent links before producing frontend output. Release tests exercise all four invalid graph cases and verify that failed builds preserve previous local output. Frontend assets use relative URLs and external scripts for Marina's content security policy. No private task payloads or traces are published.

The [public tree](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/d3b5517a-c119-4fd9-999d-362183422bf3/) currently serves [revision 6](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/d3b5517a-c119-4fd9-999d-362183422bf3/v/6/), published October 19. The source release safeguards and maintenance instructions apply to subsequent releases; merging alone does not change the live applet selection.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[taskcompendium] Remove the cache shard-count test (#10263)

Remove the campaign cache compaction test and its unused imports. It
requires exactly two descriptor shards before explicit compaction, but
FineStore can already merge those shards when a writer closes.

FineStore covers compaction and persisted values. TaskCompendium retains
coverage for request reuse, invalid cache entries, and cache storage
failures.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Move marin-finelog-server into the controller extra (#10236)

marin-iris listed the 38 MiB native marin-finelog-server wheel as a base
dependency, so every root `uv run` (even `fsutil cp`) installed it. Only
the
controller and LocalCluster load the embedded log server, and
`finelog.embedded` already raises an install hint when it is missing.

The wheel now lives in the `controller` extra, which the controller
image and
infra/pulumi already install. The iris and zephyr test groups depend on
`marin-iris[controller]` so the version floor stays in one place. Local
`iris cluster start --local` now needs `--package marin-iris --extra
controller`; the README shows it.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
Clarify Finelog outage behavior in hero alert runbooks (#10257)

Clarify that retryable Finelog query failures produce non-firing rows
for hero run alerts. `FinelogFleetUnhealthy` reports the shared
query-path failure. Empty and invalid bridge responses still use
Grafana's no-data and execution-error states.

The loss-spike runbook now also distinguishes `healthy` from
`warming_up` after the sample minimums are met.
